lead_headline: No new restaurant leads detected today — first zero-lead day in weeks as holiday weekend slows the intelligence pipeline.

restaurant.blurb: 0 new leads today. Active leads: 268 (147 openings, 121 closures). The tracker goes dark for the first time this quarter.

liquor.blurb: Zero applications again — the freeze now hits 36 days with no bar, restaurant, or retail license filings since early June. The July 4 holiday extends the longest application drought on record. The 12,325-license database historically sees 2-4 weekly applications even during summer lulls, making this six-week silence anomalous. Whether driven by holiday closures, capital constraints, or administrative bottlenecks, the pipeline remains frozen. The next filing will reset the clock on what's become the most significant licensing slowdown in tracker history.

reputation.blurb: 4 mentions yesterday — Facebook drove 3 of 4 pickups, circulating stories on Denver democratic socialist strategy, downtown office vacancies, and mayoral politics. The Kiro mayoral speculation and downtown office crisis narratives fueled the week's strongest engagement, overtaking the Luxonis funding announcement and Aldi expansion coverage.

subscriptions.blurb: Net −1 yesterday (0 new, 1 canceled) holds MTD at +8, still running +2.7/day for July. 90-day net: +132. The second consecutive day of negative net (−1 Wed, −1 Thu) follows last week's explosive +26 run that reversed June's stagnation. The 7-day window still shows strength (+26 net vs. prior week's −6), but the two-day pause suggests the late-June surge may be cooling. July's pace (+2.7/day) still outperforms the YTD baseline (+1.3/day), and the 90-day trend remains strongly positive. Whether this week's slowdown is holiday-related or signals momentum loss will clarify by Monday.
